# Playing XI — How It Works

This is where you build and configure the team that steps onto the pitch. Every choice here directly affects how your team performs in matches.

## Team Level Overview

At the top of the page you can see the current **Batting**, **Bowling**, and **Fielding** levels of your Playing XI, as well as the **Overall** team level. These numbers reflect the combined strength of your selected 11 players and update live as you make changes.

## The Two Main Action Buttons

- **Auto Build** — Automatically picks the best possible XI from your entire squad. It accounts for all conditions: home player requirements, minimum squad rules, legend limits, maximum caps, and your currently selected formation. It also sets the optimal bowling order at the same time.
- **Reserve** — Opens a bottom drawer showing every player on your bench. You can drag and drop a bench player into the XI to replace an existing one. A player can only replace another player **of the same role** — for example, an all-rounder can only be swapped with another all-rounder, a bowler with a bowler.

## Prepare

The **Prepare** section shows your team's readiness status for the upcoming match, including any outstanding tasks you need to complete before the game starts.

## Tactical Balance XI

This section evaluates your XI against **12 criteria** to help you build a well-rounded, tactically sound team. Tap the meter to open a modal showing all twelve criteria and how your current XI scores against each one.

Example criteria include:

- At least **one leg spinner** who ranks within the top 6 players by bowling level
- At least **one left-arm pace** bowler
- At least **one right-arm pace** bowler
- At least **one off-spinner**
- At least **one genuine all-rounder**
- No more than **two wicket-keepers** in the XI
- At least **one left-handed** batsman
- At least **one right-handed** batsman
- No player placed **outside their designated position**

Meeting all twelve criteria gives you a fully balanced Playing XI ready for any match situation.

## The Two Tabs

- **Batting tab** — Manage your 11 playing slots and batting order.
- **Bowling tab** — Set your over-by-over bowling lineup. Assign a bowler to each of the 10 over slots. No bowler can bowl consecutive overs, and each has a maximum over quota. A red dot on the Bowling tab means your bowling order is incomplete — fix it before the match.

## The Playing XI Cards

Your 11 players are displayed in **batting order** — the player in slot 1 bats first, the player in slot 11 bats last.

There are three batting position zones, and they **overlap** at their boundaries:

- **Top Order** — positions 1 to 4
- **Middle Order** — positions 4 to 8
- **Lower Order** — positions 8 to 11

Each player has a preferred zone based on their role. If a player is placed **outside their preferred zone**, they receive a **−2 batting penalty** during the match.

### Interacting with Player Cards

- **Drag and drop** cards to reorder the batting lineup — changes are saved automatically.
- **Tap a card** to open a quick-view modal showing the player's basic stats and similar players sitting on the bench. Tap a bench player **twice** to swap them into that slot.
- Each filled slot has a **✕** button to remove the player back to the reserve bench.
- Empty slots show a placeholder — tap it to open the Reserve drawer and pick a replacement.

## Bottom Action Bar

At the bottom of the page you will find several controls, from left to right:

### Formation

Shows your current squad formation — for example **5 · 2 · 4** means 5 batsmen, 2 all-rounders, 4 bowlers. Tap it to open the formation selector, which lists all formations available based on your current squad. Each formation also shows the **over quota** for bowlers. The formation that best suits your squad is displayed at the top.

### Batting Strategy

Choose how your team approaches batting during a match:

- **Conservative** — Prioritises staying at the crease. Very low risk of wickets but never plays aggressively.
- **Standard** — A balanced, defensive game. A safe and consistent choice for most situations.
- **Attacking** — Balances defensive and aggressive shot selection. Higher chance of big runs but also a greater risk of losing wickets.

### Autoplay

The **Autoplay** toggle lets you set your team to play automatically, with the system controlling your innings decisions. Turn it off to play manually and make your own choices ball by ball.

### Captain

The **Captain badge** shows your current captain's name. Tap it to open the captain selector and choose a different captain from your Playing XI. Your captain must always be one of the 11 selected players.

### Super Over

The **Super Over** button manages your squad for tie-breaker super overs.

- A **green indicator** means your Super Over squad is fully configured.
- Assign exactly **3 batsmen** and **1 bowler** — all must come from your current Playing XI.
- If a match ends in a tie, the selected players are **automatically used** in the Super Over.
- You can also manually select players from your team at any point before the match.
- The same player can fill both the batter and bowler roles if they are an all-rounder.
- If no squad is set, the system auto-selects your top 3 batsmen by batting level and your top bowler by bowling level.

## Team Rules You Must Follow

- Exactly **11 players** in the XI.
- At least **1 wicket-keeper**.
- At least **5 players** with a bowling rating above 0.
- The captain must be one of the 11 players.
- Your league may require a minimum number of **home country players** in the XI.
- Your league may limit how many **legend players** can appear in the XI at once.

## Tips

1. Use **Auto Build** after signing new players to keep the XI optimal, then fine-tune manually.
2. Check the **Tactical Balance** meter before every match and fix any failing criteria.
3. Put your strongest batsmen at positions **1–4** and hard-hitters at **7–9**.
4. Keep your **best bowlers** for the powerplay (overs 1–2) and death overs (9–10).
5. Check the **Bowling tab** before every match — an incomplete bowling order means your team cannot bowl properly.
6. Plan your **Super Over squad** in advance: your three best finishers as batters and your most reliable death-overs bowler.
7. Use **Attacking** strategy when chasing a large total; switch to **Conservative** when protecting a small lead.
